title: Edith and Lena Wilson, Adelaide Hall and Black Broadway
summary: Lena is Edith Wilson's sister; Edith was the original Aunt Jemima.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You were saying about Lena Wilson, you think she's Edith Wilson's sister.

Yes, she is Edith Wilson's sister -- Edith Wilson who is the famous artist from the early -- about the turn of the century and I saw Edith -- Edith is now appearing with the Black Broadway production.
Are they touring now, the Black Broadway, they're not playing here in New York (inaudible).

Adelaide had to go back to, Adelaide went into Michael's Pub for a while and then she's in -- the last time I saw her she said she had to go back to London, but I think Adelaide wants to come back to the States and so somebody is working on bookings for her.
Well, Edith Wilson was also on television for many years, selling her face to a pancake company.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
That's right, she was the original Aunt Jemima. You know she was the person who represented the Aunt Jemima on the pancake flour box. Also, I guess in personal appearances.
Did she do television? I mean, would she appear in commercials?
No, no, because they have -- this was before television, you know. Maybe on radio, but not on television.
All right, it goes that far back.

Oh, yes, she was no longer -- she may have been billed as the original Aunt Jemima in her personal appearances. You know she toured a lot with Butterbeans and Susie and she did what they call the TOBA circuit. She was quite successful and quite popular.
